propositions: Core must execute five push-first retry cycles with fetch-and-merge recovery only after retriable rejection, followed by exactly one conditional terminal push only if the fifth rejection produced a clean merge.

Strict delivery raises catchable PushDeliveryError with pinned reason, git detail, and unpushed-commit count; best-effort default preserves legacy warning-and-return behavior for all existing callers.
Python module adapter translates PushDeliveryError to stderr and nonzero exit at process boundary without writing ticket events or BRIDGE_ALERT.
All legacy callers (event append, batch append, import, close, delete, compact, claim) must omit strict or reach core with strict=False to retain best-effort disposition.
Strict failure does not modify ticket events, HEAD state, working tree, or emit BRIDGE_ALERT; policy declines are distinct from transport failures.
